questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: In the direction you want the trailer to move.
In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to move.
To the left until backing is complete.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to move.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel the opposite way from where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the wheel the other way to follow it.

questions.question: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away, what happens?

options.text: The trailer will stop normally.
The trailer will have no brakes.
The trailer will speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will have no brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers without spring brakes will lose all braking power if the air supply leaks out. The wheels will spin freely with no brakes to stop them.

questions.question: After completing a pre-trip inspection, what should you check?

options.text: The service line valve is closed.
The trailer hand brake is applied.
The emergency line valve is open.

questions.correctAnswerText: The service line valve is closed.
questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency and service line valves to check that air reaches all brakes. Listen for escaping air. Then close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: If the trailer drifts off-course while backing, what should you do?

options.text: Return the steering wheel to the 12 o'clock position.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the drift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, correct it right away by turning the top of the steering wheel toward the direction of the drift.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: To test the trailer brakes.
To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.
To accelerate.

questions.correctAnswerText: To test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only for testing. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: What do shut-off valves do?

options.text: Prevent air from escaping air brake systems.
Prevent air from entering air brake systems.
Override vehicles that are out of control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent air from escaping air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control the flow of air between trailers. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed to keep air in the braking system.

questions.question: When backing to couple a trailer, how should the tractor be positioned?

options.text: Directly in front of the trailer.
Directly next to the trailer.
Parallel with the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor directly in front of the trailer when coupling. Backing at an angle can cause the trailer to move and damage the landing gear.

questions.question: Where should cargo be placed to prevent a rollover?

options.text: As high as possible inside a trailer.
As low as possible inside a trailer.
On the driver's side of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible inside a trailer.
questions.explanation: Heavy cargo high up makes a vehicle more likely to roll over. Keep cargo weight as low as possible in the trailer to reduce this risk.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor without a trailer.
A tractor attached to two trailers.
A tractor with a tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: A tractor without a trailer.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor operating without a semi-trailer. Drivers should be careful when operating bobtail tractors.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, which trailer should be directly behind the cab?

options.text: The lightest one.
The heaviest one.
The smallest one.

questions.correctAnswerText: The heaviest one.
questions.explanation: The heaviest trailer should be positioned closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should be at the rear.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
A valve that prevents a truck from being stolen
A valve that prevents the driver from driving too fast

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. The valve closes automatically when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: Which of the following will not help prevent a rig from rolling over?

options.text: Keeping the cargo as close to the ground as possible
Driving slowly around turns
Driving on the shoulder of a road

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving on the shoulder of a road
questions.explanation: To prevent a rig from rolling over, keep cargo weight as low as possible and drive slowly around turns. Driving on the shoulder does not help prevent rollover.

questions.question: If you are not sure if a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle
Assume it has ABS

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes
questions.explanation: To find out if a trailer has ABS, look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes.

questions.question: A tractor protection valve:

options.text: Keeps air in a brake system if there is a bad leak
Prevents a truck from being stolen
Prevents a trailer from being accidentally released

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in a brake system if there is a bad leak
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. The valve closes automatically when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: During a trip, landing gear should be:

options.text: Completely raised
Completely lowered
Skimming the pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: Completely raised
questions.explanation: Landing gear should always be completely raised before driving. If landing gear is not fully raised, it could catch on railroad tracks or other hazards on the road.

questions.question: When the wheels of a trailer lock up:

options.text: The trailer will be drivable
The trailer may swing around
The vehicle will maintain steering

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer may swing around
questions.explanation: When trailer wheels lock up, the trailer may swing out and hit other vehicles. This is especially likely when the trailer is lightly loaded.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle goes around a corner:

options.text: The vehicle must use at least two lanes
The front and rear wheels will move in different paths
It is best to allow the rear wheels to drive over the curb

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels will move in different paths
questions.explanation: When a vehicle goes around a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking and is especially noticeable with trailers.

questions.question: The service air line is often controlled by the foot brake and is attached to the ____ valves.

options.text: Relay
Supply
Emergency

questions.correctAnswerText: Relay
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. The service air line connects to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: When driving while pulling trailers, you should:

options.text: Make sudden turns with the steering wheel
Avoid making sudden moves
Push the accelerator to the floor when starting from a stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden moves
questions.explanation: Always steer gently and smoothly when pulling a trailer. Sudden steering moves could cause the trailer to tip over.

questions.question: Operating combination vehicles usually requires ____ operating single vehicles.

options.text: Less skill than
About the same level of skill as
More skill than

questions.correctAnswerText: More skill than
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single vehicles. Operating a combination vehicle requires more driving skill than operating a single commercial vehicle.
